intro: A gallery mount makes carving and surface easy to see. The makers and the performances that gave each mask meaning belong to different communities and histories.
alt: Three separate carved masks in museum mounts beside the modern visitor.

variants.name: Dan mask
variants.look: The smooth, dark surface highlights the mask's oval face and the restrained shaping around its eyes and mouth.
variants.history: Dan communities live in present-day Liberia and Côte d’Ivoire. Different masks belong to different performance roles.
variants.when: Study the smooth planes when considering what makes a face expressive with very few details.
variants.why: The dark surface and fine transitions encourage close looking and make the features feel deliberate.

variants.name: Fang mask
variants.look: The light face stretches into a long oval, with high arched brows and a pronounced nose.
variants.history: Certain Fang masks from regions including present-day Gabon are associated with the Ngil society. Fang masks also take other forms and served other functions.
variants.when: Compare face length, brow and color to see which formal choices make the example distinctive.
variants.why: A long uninterrupted face gives greater emphasis to the brow and central ridge.

variants.name: Pende mask
variants.look: Pigmented planes and sharply shaped facial features stand out from the wood.
variants.history: Pende masquerades in what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo have included a wide range of characters, occasions and mask types.
variants.when: Look for the way carved angles make a face readable in a performance setting.
variants.why: Pronounced planes can register changes of movement and light across the face.

prompt: Create a triptych of THREE separate equally sized square frames in a single 3:1 horizontal row (two clearly visible thin white dividers between the frames). For an arts learning site about differences between three culturally distinct historical woodcarving traditions. In each square, place a foreground profile portrait of the same adult female modern visitor in the near lower left corner: ash-blonde hair low bun, colored square clip, black rectangular glasses, elegant charcoal suit jacket over black knee-length dress, bright blue lanyard badge, white coffee mug with small four-color squares. Show full upright museum display of a SINGLE distinct mask on the right in each square with separate exhibit lighting and backdrops. Left black smooth oval Dan mask with subtle face planes in a neutral gray exhibit; center tall elongated pale heart-faced Fang mask with pronounced vertical nose ridge in warmer brown exhibit; right angular triangular red and cream Pende mask in a cool gray-blue exhibit. One clear instance of woman and one clear mask per square. Gallery visitors only, no costumes or reenactment, no text or titles or captions.
